source.name: Mathematics Subject Classification 2020
source.scope: All 63 two-digit MSC2020 classes, used only as a breadth-audit checklist
source.license_note: Only class codes are reproduced. MSC labels and hierarchy are not imported; mapping notes are original OLA analysis.

method: A covered code has one or more active OLA territories that expose its mathematical terrain at the atlas educational resolution.
A downstream-interface code is represented by mathematical methods and interfaces, while nonmathematical domain knowledge remains outside this base map.
An excluded-nonterrain code classifies history or education about mathematics rather than mathematical knowledge or capability terrain.
Crosswalk membership does not import MSC ordering, definitions, hierarchy, prerequisites, or instructional assumptions.

entries.note: General mathematical work is represented through cross-cutting abstraction and modeling terrain; publication collections are not imported.
History and biography concern mathematics but are not mathematical knowledge or capability terrain in this base map.
Logic, set, model, type, proof, and category foundations are explicit territories.
Counting, combinatorial structures, graphs, and networks are explicit terrain.
Order, lattices, and general algebra provide the corresponding terrain.
General algebraic systems are represented across general algebra and major algebraic structures.
Divisibility and number theory are explicit terrain.
Polynomial and field structures are represented across two algebra territories.
Commutative algebra is aggregated within ring, module, and polynomial terrain at this resolution.
Algebraic geometry shares an explicit territory with differential geometry at the atlas resolution.
Vector, matrix, linear, and multilinear structures are separately visible.
Associative rings and algebras are aggregated within the major-structures territory.
Nonassociative structures are represented at a broader algebraic-structures resolution.
Category and related proof foundations are explicit terrain.
K-theoretic terrain is visible through category foundations and topology, though not a standalone territory.
Group theory is explicit within the major-structures territory.
Topological and Lie group terrain is represented across algebraic and differential-geometric territories.
Real-function terrain spans function families, continuity, differentiation, and integration.
Measure and integration are explicit in the revised advanced-analysis split.
Complex analysis is an explicit territory.
Potential-theoretic terrain is aggregated within complex analysis at this resolution.
Several-variable and analytic-space terrain is aggregated within complex analysis.
Special-function terrain is represented through function families and series.
Ordinary differential equations are explicit within a differential-equations territory.
Partial differential equations are explicit within a differential-equations territory.
Dynamical systems are named within the differential-equations territory.
Difference and functional equations are represented through recurrence and differential-equation terrain.
Sequences and series are an explicit territory.
Approximation is explicit within numerical analysis.
Harmonic analysis is explicit in the revised advanced-analysis split.
Abstract harmonic analysis is represented in the harmonic-and-operator territory.
Transform and operational terrain is represented in the harmonic-and-operator territory.
Integral-equation terrain spans inverse-problem and operator-analysis structures.
Functional analysis is explicit in the revised advanced-analysis split.
Operator theory is explicit in the harmonic-and-operator territory.
Variational, optimal-control, and optimization terrain spans two explicit territories.
Synthetic and coordinate geometry are separately visible.
Convex, discrete, and computational geometry is an explicit territory.
Differential geometry is explicitly named.
General topology is represented within the topology-and-manifolds territory.
Algebraic topology spans topology and category-foundational terrain at this resolution.
Manifolds and cell-complex terrain is represented within topology and manifolds.
Global analysis on manifolds spans differential geometry and topology terrain.
Probability distributions and stochastic processes are explicit terrain.
Statistical modeling, inference, and multivariate or computational statistics are explicit.
Numerical analysis, numerical linear algebra, and error representation are explicit.
Theoretical computer science, computability, complexity, and symbolic computation are explicit.
The mathematical structures of mechanics are mapped; physical domain knowledge remains downstream.
Continuum and solid-mechanics mathematics is represented at the application interface.
Fluid-mechanics mathematics is represented at the application interface.
Mathematical structures used in optics and electromagnetism are represented through mathematical physics.
Thermal and transfer models are represented through mechanics and mathematical-physics interfaces.
Quantum-theoretic mathematics is represented through mathematical physics.
Statistical-mechanical mathematics is represented through mathematical physics.
Relativistic and gravitational mathematics is represented through mathematical physics.
Astronomical and space-science mathematics is represented at an application interface.
Geophysical mathematics is represented at an earth-and-environment interface.
Operations research and continuous and discrete optimization are explicit.
Game-theoretic, economic, financial, and social-system mathematics is an explicit interface.
Biological and medical mathematics is an explicit application interface.
Systems, control, and inverse-problem mathematics is explicit terrain.
Coding and information theory is an explicit territory.
Mathematics education concerns the teaching and learning of mathematics; curricula and pedagogy are downstream overlays, not canonical terrain.
